tex_content.html:
Lemma
↗ cor:gradient-radial-distance ↗ prop:coordinate-representations-divergence-laplacian 1. ch11:11.13

Let $(x^i)$ be Riemannian normal coordinates on a normal neighborhood $U$ of $p$, let $r$ be radial distance, and let $\det g=\det (g_{ij})$. On $U\setminus \{ p\} $, \begin{equation} \Delta r=\partial _r\log \bigl(r^{n-1}\sqrt{\det g}\bigr). \tag {11.23} \end{equation}

Proof

\sketch The Gauss lemma gives

\[ \operatorname {grad}r=\partial _r, \qquad g^{ij}\partial _jr=\frac{x^i}{r}. \]

The coordinate Laplacian formula yields

\begin{align*} \Delta r & =\frac1{\sqrt{\det g}} \partial _i\left(g^{ij}\sqrt{\det g}\, \partial _jr\right)\\ & =\partial _i\left(\frac{x^i}{r}\right) +\frac{x^i}{r\sqrt{\det g}}\partial _i\sqrt{\det g}\\ & =\frac{n-1}{r} +\frac1{\sqrt{\det g}}\partial _r\sqrt{\det g}, \end{align*}

which is (11.23).

□

Günther's comparison theorem \cite{Gun60} gives the sectional-curvature volume estimate and its equality case.
